[{"id":533077014,"iid":3927,"project_id":34675721,"title":"feat(df): add nuget proxy matcher","description":"Adds `NuGetMatcher`, the proxy classifier for the NuGet ecosystem. Nothing on `main` uses it yet; the `glab df nuget` command follows in a separate MR.

- **Downloads:** v3 flatcontainer URLs (`…/{id}/{version}/{id}.{version}.nupkg`). A `.nupkg` download outside that shape, such as a nuget.org v2 CDN URL, fails closed. Coordinates carry the id and version as the URL spells them; NuGet clients lowercase flatcontainer paths.
- **Pushes:** recognized by body rather than path, because each server advertises its own push URL. A multipart PUT counts as a push when one of its parts is a zip archive (`.nupkg` or `.snupkg`). The coordinate comes from the manifest NuGet would use: the single root-level `.nuspec`, with exactly one `<metadata>`, `<id>` and `<version>`, read with a 1 MiB cap. Packages larger than the in-memory inspection window are read from the spilled body. A package without a usable manifest, or a push carrying two packages, fails closed. Multipart PUTs with no zip part are forwarded. Push coordinates keep the casing in the package's nuspec.
- **Not covered:** v2 downloads (`…/package/{id}/{version}`) and non-multipart PUTs are forwarded uninspected, since neither has a shape the matcher can tell apart from other traffic. nuget.org's v2 feed redirects downloads to a `.nupkg` CDN URL, which fails closed. NuGet clients always push `multipart/form-data`.
- Blocked NuGet requests get a JSON 403 body (`block.go`).

Known gap: the policy backend matches NuGet names case-sensitively, while most stored NuGet names are mixed case, so lowercase download coordinates can miss advisories and licenses. That needs a backend change: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/633750.

## Testing

End to end with real `dotnet` (SDK 8.0.425, Linux arm64) through a scratch build of this branch with the nuget command wiring from `feat/dependency-firewall`. Downloads came from nuget.org, pushes went to a local HTTPS BaGetter feed, and verdicts came from the fake policy checker.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `dotnet restore` Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3 | restored; checked `newtonsoft.json@13.0.3` |
| same, with it blocked | restore fails with 403 |
| restore Serilog.Sinks.Console 5.0.1 | package and dependency `serilog@3.1.1` checked |
| `dotnet nuget push` Demo.Pkg 1.0.0 | pushed; checked `Demo.Pkg@1.0.0` |
| push Demo.Pkg 1.0.1 while blocked | 403; not stored |
| push with `.snupkg`; the `.snupkg` alone while blocked | both pushed; symbols push alone gets 403 |
| push an 84 MB package (past the 64 MiB window) | checked and stored |
| multipart PUT of a test report | forwarded |
| multipart PUT of a zip with no `.nuspec` | 403, unparseable |
| decoy package (nested `Benign` nuspec before root `Evil`), Evil blocked | 403, checked as `Evil@1.0.0` |
| same decoy through the matcher before 01d2605c2 | pushed; the feed stored it as `Evil` write kubeconfig to real home in snap","description":"## Description

Under strict snap confinement, snapd rewrites `HOME` to `$SNAP_USER_DATA`. client-go builds the default kubeconfig path from `HOME`, so `glab cluster agent update-kubeconfig` wrote to `~/snap/glab/<rev>/.kube/config`, reported `Updated context ...`, and left `~/.kube/config` untouched. This follows the root-cause analysis in the issue triage comment.

This MR:

- Resolves the default kubeconfig against `SNAP_REAL_HOME` when it is set. `KUBECONFIG` and `--kubeconfig` still take precedence, unchanged.
- Adds a `kube-config` plug (`personal-files` interface, write access to `$HOME/.kube`) to `snap/snapcraft.yaml`, because the `home` plug excludes hidden files.
- When running under snap and reading or writing the kubeconfig fails with `permission denied`, appends a hint to run `sudo snap connect glab:kube-config`. Without the plug connected, the command now fails loudly instead of reporting success.

Note for maintainers: `personal-files` is a super-privileged interface. The Snap Store must approve it before upload, and it is not auto-connected, so users must run `sudo snap connect glab:kube-config` (same as the existing `password-manager-service` plug). Until the store approves it, the `export KUBECONFIG=~/kubeconfig` workaround from the issue still applies. If you'd rather ship the Go change on its own first, the snapcraft change can be split out.

## Related Issues

Closes #8304

## How has this been tested?

- New command-level tests in `agent_update_kubeconfig_test.go`, using `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest` and client-go mocks:
  - with `SNAP_REAL_HOME` set, the context goes to `$SNAP_REAL_HOME/.kube/config`
  - `KUBECONFIG` and `--kubeconfig` still win over `SNAP_REAL_HOME`
  - a read or write `permission denied` under snap shows the `snap connect` hint, and the same error outside snap does not
  - outside snap, the default path is still client-go's `RecommendedHomeFile`
- `go test ./internal/commands/cluster/...`, `golangci-lint run ./internal/commands/cluster/agent/...`, `go run ./scripts/comment-overlap -threshold 1.0 -max-findings 0` on the changed files, and `go build ./...`.
- The snap package itself is not built or installed in this MR.
